method: One assistant analyst read closing sequences and consulted earlier action when needed. Ending-family and sacrifice labels are interpretations; phrase flags are exact case-insensitive whole-word/phrase matches within the final 250 whitespace-delimited words.
scope: 22 manual texts, 45 recent formal OH, 48 recent baselines, 20 recovered historical formal OH, 48 historical baselines; 1 additional historical diagnostic version separate. Six original August Local completions were not recovered. Canaries and other diagnostic generations excluded.
sacrifice_code: For the 67 core OH stories only: an enacted lasting cost in life, memory, capacity, liberty or power to protect others; ordinary risk, lost aspirations, grief and forced enemy consumption excluded. Broader than a literal self-versus-world binary. Other strata not scored.

entries.title: Neon Echoes

entries.prompt: Write a suspense story that takes place in one location over one night. It must contain no weapons and no supernatural explanation. Build escalating danger from ordinary objects, human decisions, and limited information, then resolve the threat without breaking those constraints.
entries.ending: Cold defeats the intruder, revealed as a displaced deep-sea animal; Elias survives and restores ordinary warmth.

entries.title: The Weight of the Hourglass
entries.prompt: Write a quiet literary story with no villain, no death, and no twist ending. Create meaningful change through observation, relationship, and choice rather than danger, and conclude with an earned shift that does not depend on a hidden revelation.
entries.ending: Julian welcomes Clara's disruption, leaves the archives for a walk with her, and accepts unpreserved time.

As they stepped out into the crisp evening air, Julian didn't worry about the wind or the dampness of the air. He simply walked, feeling the weight of the hour glass turn, happy to be moving forward into the unpredictable, unpreserved light of the world.

entries.title: The Weight of the Gilded Key
entries.prompt: Write a tragedy in which the protagonist succeeds at the goal they openly pursue and, through that success, destroys what actually mattered to them. The outcome must follow from understandable choices, and the story must prepare both the victory and its cost.
entries.ending: Elias restores the Orrery but loses his companion; sustaining the perfect machine now imprisons him in solitude.
entries.closing_250_words_whitespace_normalized: in the sudden silence of the house, it sounded like a gavel. Elias stood frozen. He looked back at the Orrery. The machine was magnificent. It was a triumph of engineering, a beacon of gold and obsidian spinning in perfect, eternal harmony. It would continue to track the stars with unerring accuracy for ten thousand years. It was the most valuable object in the hemisphere. He reached out to touch the brass arm of Earth, and as he did, he realized the crushing weight of his success. The Orrery required constant maintenance; the palladium key was volatile and needed precise calibration every few hours to prevent the gears from grinding themselves to dust. To keep the victory alive, he would have to stay here. He would have to live in the silence of the estate, tending to the machine that had cost him his soul. He had chased the key to unlock his future, only to find that the lock had been on his own heart, and he had spent the only currency that mattered to buy a clock that told him exactly how many seconds he had spent alone. Elias sat on the cold floor of the ballroom, the golden light of the mechanical sun washing over him, and listened to the rhythmic, indifferent ticking of the most perfect machine in the world. He had achieved his goal. He was the master of the Orrery, and he was the only person left in the house to hear it breathe.
